extracted.intended_audience: proofreaders, copyholders, and production staff at book publishers (e.g., University of Chicago Press)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and standards for copyholders and proofreaders on how to read, mark, handle, and dispatch proofs and for general house style (capitalization, punctuation, italics, hyphenation, numbering, etc.). Intended to govern day-to-day proofreading/production tasks in a publishing house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaim responsibility under urgent orders
rubrics_metrics.description: When orders are imperative, protect yourself by letting it be understood that you have done your best in the time allotted you, but that you must disclaim any further responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear when time constraints prevent full checking; communicate that work was done to best ability within limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial every galley
rubrics_metrics.description: Put your initial at the top of every galley you read or revise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saves time tracing proofs and ensures credit for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading voice for copyholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate a low, soft, clear reading-voice; only your own proofreader has to hear you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep voice low so as not to disturb others; clarity and steadiness aid accurate proofreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to small words as much as large ones
rubrics_metrics.description: From the proofreader's point of view, the small words are as essential as the big ones. Get them all in — and get them in right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not skim function words; omissions or wrong small words change meaning and create errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enunciate plural -s distinctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Enunciate your plural s's distinctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear pronunciation helps the proofreader catch plurality errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept requests to repeat or inspect copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not get offended when your reader asks you to repeat, or to look at the copy for himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperate with proofreader's checks; it improves accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate reading speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulate and equalize your speed. Do not race at a break‑neck pace through typewritten copy while fumbling through manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent pace appropriate to the medium (typed vs manuscript) to avoid missing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make careful guesses about illegible words
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not keep guessing at a word. Look at it closely, consider the context, and do not speak it until you have made it out — or at least the very best guess of which you are capable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify uncertain readings before passing them along; avoid introducing new errors by careless guessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning relative to reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Sit at right angles to your reader, if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will be heard better and can watch the proofreader's hand more easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time for corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Give your reader a chance to make his corrections. Slow up the moment he puts his pencil to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents re-reading the same ground twice and ensures corrections are captured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a signaling system
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolve your own system of signals. Do not, for instance, waste time by saying 'in italics' for every word or letter so treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brief cues (raise voice, tap table once per word, or both). The code need only be intelligible to you and your reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not waste time on style queries during reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not waste time over matters of style. The proofreader is supposed to know the rules without your telling him; for instance, what titles are to be set in italics, and what roman-quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve style discussions for separate queries; during reading, assume house rules and let proofreader apply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer marks carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful in transferring marks. A mark in the wrong place means two errors uncorrected in place of one corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure marks are placed exactly where intended; misplaced marks can multiply errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check contents before sending proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: In sending out proofs, see that everything is there. Arrange the copy and proof-sheets neatly and consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify completeness and logical order to prevent missing pages or mis-sequenced proofs being sent out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult job ticket before sending proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Never send out proofs without consulting the job ticket for the number wanted, and the name and address of the person to whom they are to be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow job ticket exactly to meet quantity and recipient requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include correct supporting materials with proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should accompany the galley-proof; the foul proof (author's marked galley-proof) should accompany the page-proof. In case no galley-proof has been sent, the manuscript should accompany the page-proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always bundle appropriate earlier stages or marked copies with subsequent proofs so corrections can be checked in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label envelopes with contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate in the lower left-hand corner the contents of all the envelopes you address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear external labeling speeds processing and prevents misplacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fasten pins at top center
rubrics_metrics.description: Fasten your pins in the center at the top, not diagonally in the left-hand corner, thus covering up the directions, etc., often written there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid covering job directions or addresses with pins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return reference volumes nightly
rubrics_metrics.description: Return every evening to the file or the bookcase any volume that may have been taken out for reference during the day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains shared resource availability and order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain proofroom housekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that you are the housekeeper of the proof-room, and take pride in its neat and orderly appearance. Keeping the records, files, etc., naturally devolves upon you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perfect your system so that everything can be located at a moment's notice; proactive organization increases appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader's marks (list and meanings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard marks for indicating editorial corrections: dele (delete), letter reversed (turn), put in space, close up (no space), bad spacing, wrong font, transpose, make a new paragraph, indent/put in em-quad, carry left/right, elevate, imperfect type—correct, space shows between words—push down, straighten crooked line, straighten alignment, restore words crossed out, print ligature, indicate omitted words in copy, query to author, put in capitals/small capitals/lower case, put in roman/italic/bold-face type, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conventional symbols consistently so compositors and typesetters can apply corrections unambiguously; include examples and ensure marks are placed precisely where change is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and placement of errata and 'for and read' notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Words for and read are to be italicized in errata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow house conventions for errata formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization rules (broad categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalization covering proper nouns, adjectives derived from proper nouns, names of organizations, governmental departments, sessions of Congress, historical and geological epochs, titles, and many miscellaneous categories (see sections 1–57 and word lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the manual's detailed capitalization rules by category (e.g., geographic names, book titles, institutional names); consult specific sections for edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for italics: used for titles of books/works, emphasis, certain foreign words and phrases, names of genera/species, letters designating unknown quantities, continuation words ('continued'), and other specified items (see rules 58–73).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overuse italics; some long bibliographies may omit italics per house practice. Use italics for emphatic or conventional purposes as listed in detailed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and compound words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for hyphenization of compounds and division of words, including compounds with particular prefixes/suffixes (co-, re-, non-, semi-, ex-, vice-, etc.), compounds of family terms (father, mother, brother), and many special compound classes (rules 182–214).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the manual's lists and rules; avoid unnecessary division at line-ends and treat common-element omissions with hyphenation as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive comma rules: where to use or omit commas with conjunctions, appositional clauses, adverbial clauses, parenthetical clauses, enumerations, numbers, dates, signatures, and other constructions (rules 141–162).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply context-sensitive comma rules; consult examples for clauses, serial uses, and number formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colon usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and rules for colon usage: to introduce statements, extracts, lists, between place of publication and publisher, after salutatory phrases, and to emphasize close connections between clauses (rules 131–136).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colon to signal introduction or emphasis per enumerated acceptable functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes (en- and em-) and their uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for dashes: em-dash for interruptions/parenthetical elements/ 'to' in time; en-dash for ranges and certain compounds; dashes for emphasis, summarizing clauses, and indicating change in sentence (rules 166–175).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose dash size by function (em vs en) and follow spacing/usage conventions in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for numbers: when to spell out, when to use figures, treatment of round numbers, use of comma for thousands, treatment of consecutive numbers and ranges (rules 94–98, 159, 173).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set consistent numeric style for reading matter vs technical listings; use en-dash for ranges when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures, tables, and columns formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for columns of figures, spacing of columns, table headings, open tables, use of leaders and double rules, and when columns of averages/generalizations may be set in distinctive type (various sections referenced: 241–250).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow table and tabular rules for spacing, leaders, and typographic emphasis to facilitate readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes and indices
rubrics_metrics.description: General style for footnotes (numbering, placing of index figure, sequence, and rules 232–239) and indices (rules for indexing, use of 'See'/'See also' italicizing, treatment of particles/prefixes, 240).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number and place footnote indicators per machine/platform conventions (e.g., linotype/monotype notes); follow indexing rules for alphabetization and cross-references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation and citation treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for quoting authors (when consecutive quotations follow each other), reduction of citations, punctuation of quotations, and handling of brief quotations or maxims (sections referenced: 74–87, 112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat quoted material consistently (quoted punctuation, reduction rules) and apply citation conventions for consecutive or interleaved citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses and omission marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for ellipses: how to indicate omissions, treat ellipses as part of a quotation, and when to use ellipsis vs brackets for omitted material (rules 180–181, use 178 for brackets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ellipses reflect omitted content accurately and observe spacing/placement conventions in quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation: exclamation and interrogation points
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of exclamation points (including to express irony or outcry) and interrogation points (rules 127–130).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for emphasis or rhetorical questions per manual rules; consider alternative punctuation for irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic definitions and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and usages for typographic measures and features (em/en/quad spaces, hair-space, kern, leading, face, font) and guidance on even spacing and hair-spacing taboo (sections 256–277).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow house typographic conventions for spacing and measurement; avoid hair-spacing except by explicit rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign words and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign words and phrases: italicize words and phrases from foreign languages used in English; quote English equivalents; treat quoted passages per foreign-language conventions (sections 59, 78, 85).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italicize non-anglicized foreign items; provide English equivalent in quotes when required by manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetizing and name-indexing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for alphabetizing names and indexing, including treatment of particles like 'de', 'van', 'Mac', and rules for separation and ordering (section 240).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified indexing conventions for sorting and entry formation.
